title: "STP: Single Touch Payroll Extended | Single Touch Payroll Standard"

The ATO defines the field as \"the total you have paid to your worker/payee from a CDEP wages grant\" and adds \"Do not include this amount in gross payments.\" The programme was an Indigenous employment scheme in which a community organisation paid participants from grant money rather than from its own revenue.","dsrc":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Income Community Development Employment Project Amount - Event payment","k":"Year-to-date payments from a Community Development Employment Projects wages grant","def":"A cumulative whole-dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, reported separately from gross payments and from allowances.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/forms-and-instructions/payg-payment-summary-individual-non-business/section-b-payment-details","lim":"The category has no successor once an employer moves to Phase 2 reporting, whose income type list carries no equivalent, so a nil in the later years of the asset is a reporting rule rather than a change in what people were paid. Under Phase 2, \"Instead of reporting a single gross amount, you must separately report: gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W, salary sacrifice\", and what stays behind is tightly drawn: \"Only pre-sacrifice amounts that are classified as ordinary time earnings (OTE) should be included as gross.\" Under Phase 1 the same column carried most of the pay packet.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/disaggregation-of-gross","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Gross amount of salary & wages income - Event payment","k":"Year-to-date gross salary and wages in a pay event","def":"A cumulative dollar amount for one payee, payer and income type within the financial year, covering ordinary hours, casual loading, shift penalties and other ordinary time earnings once Phase 2 applies.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/disaggregation-of-gross","lim":"The column is not a consistent series. STP reporting is built around a closed set of categories - gross, paid leave, allowances, overtime, bonuses and commissions, directors' fees, lump sum W and salary sacrifice under Phase 2, and the payment summary types under Phase 1 - and payroll systems need somewhere to put money that does not fit one of them. The column should be read against the named amounts beside it, not on its own.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/disaggregation-of-gross","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Income Other Amount - Event payment","k":"Year-to-date residual income amount in a pay event","def":"A cumulative dollar amount for one payee and payer within the financial year, holding reported pay that is not attributed to a named category.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Disaggregation of gross","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/disaggregation-of-gross","lim":"There is no published label of this name, so what falls into it depends on the payroll product and on the reporting phase, which makes it unsafe to compare between employers or over time. The ATO splits the reporting on that basis: \"If you report RFBA through STP there are two amount fields - 'exempt' and 'non-exempt'.\" The exemption reaches a defined set of employers - registered public benevolent institutions, government bodies whose employee works in or for a public hospital, registered health promotion charities and public ambulance services - so a figure here marks the payer as one of them, and RFB_TXBL_AMT holds the equivalent for everyone else.","dsrc":"ATO, Fringe benefits tax - a guide for employers, chapter 5 Reportable fringe benefits","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV%2FFBTGEMP%2F00006","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Reportable Fringe Benefits Exempt Amount - Event payment","k":"Reportable fringe benefits amount, section 57A exempt employer (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount grossed up at the lower, type 2 rate, which is one divided by one minus the FBT rate, or 1.8868 while that rate is 47 per cent. A zero also carries no information about benefits received, only that this payer is outside section 57A, and the $2,000 floor censors small amounts entirely, so the column cannot measure low-value benefits.","where":["pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m01","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m02","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m03","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m04","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m05","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m06","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m07","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m08","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m09","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m10","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m11","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m12","and 58 more"]},{"n":"RFB_TXBL_AMT","d":"The grossed-up value of an employee's reportable fringe benefits where the employer is an ordinary, FBT-paying one.","full":"The grossed-up value of an employee's reportable fringe benefits where the employer is an ordinary, FBT-paying one. It is the non-exempt half of the pair the ATO describes when it says the two STP fields represent \"RFBA reportable by an employer that is exempt from FBT under section 57A of the FBTAA, and RFBA reportable by an employer that is not exempt\". The custodian's word taxable refers to the employer's liability, not the employee's: the guide is explicit that the amount \"is not included in the employee's assessable income\" and is instead used to test eligibility for transfer payments, the Medicare levy surcharge, the private health insurance rebate and Division 293 tax.","dsrc":"ATO, Fringe benefits tax - a guide for employers, chapter 5 Reportable fringe benefits","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV%2FFBTGEMP%2F00006","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Reportable Fringe Benefits Taxable Amount - Event payment","k":"Reportable fringe benefits amount, employer not exempt under section 57A (dollars)","def":"A dollar amount, grossed up at the type 2 rate, covering benefits provided over the FBT year of 1 April to 31 March and reported in the income year that ends straight after it.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Fringe benefits tax - a guide for employers, chapter 5 Reportable fringe benefits","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=SAV%2FFBTGEMP%2F00006","lim":"The twelve months it describes are not the twelve months of the wages beside it, because the FBT year runs three months ahead of the financial year, so this column and gross pay on the same row cover different periods. ABS defines SA2s as \"medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)\" whose \"purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\", which makes this the practical column for setting payroll earnings against regional population, income or labour force estimates. STP_MESHBLOCK_ABS on the same row is finer and LGA_ASGS_2022 is the administrative alternative.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-2","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Geocoded SA2","k":"ASGS 2021 Statistical Area Level 2 code","def":"A nine-digit hierarchical code: one digit for state or territory, two for SA4, two for SA3 and four for the SA2. You must include separate YTD amounts you have withheld from each income type (and for income types that require a country code, for each combination of income type and country code).\" This column carries the main salary and wages total, with VA_TOTL_AMT, LABR_HIR_TOTL_AMT, WHM_TOTL_AMT and OTHR_SPCFD_TOTL_AMT holding the withholding for the other income types.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/tax-that-has-been-withheld-or-paid","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Total PAYGW Amount - Event payment","k":"Total PAYG withholding, year to date (dollars)","def":"A cumulative dollar amount within the financial year, remitted under the pay as you go withholding system and credited against the employee's assessment.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/tax-that-has-been-withheld-or-paid","lim":"Withholding is not tax paid. It is an instalment set by tax tables and by what the employee declared to the payer, so a person who claimed the wrong threshold or has several jobs can be well over or under, and the difference only settles on assessment. For foreign employment income the employer reports the residual after foreign tax, so the column understates the total collected on that income.","where":["pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m01","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m02","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m03","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m04","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m05","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m06","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m07","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m08","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m09","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m10","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m11","pmp-stp-extended / stp_extended_pay_events_2020_m12","and 58 more"]},{"n":"VA_TOTL_AMT","d":"Tax withheld year to date from an independent contractor under a voluntary agreement, so a figure here marks the worker as a contractor rather than an employee.","full":"Tax withheld year to date from an independent contractor under a voluntary agreement, so a figure here marks the worker as a contractor rather than an employee. The monthly tables span the move to STP Phase 2, which employers began from 1 January 2022 and which recast withholding from the old payment summary categories onto income types, so which of these columns is populated depends on the month and on when the payer transitioned.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/tax-that-has-been-withheld-or-paid","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Year To Date Withheld Amount - Event payment","k":"PAYG withholding, year to date (dollars)","def":"A cumulative dollar amount of pay as you go withholding within the financial year, reset at the start of each year.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Tax that has been withheld or paid","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/tax-that-has-been-withheld-or-paid","lim":"The label does not say which payments it covers, so it must not be added to TAX_WHELD_TOTL_AMT or to the income-type withholding columns before checking, month by month, which of them are filled; double counting a person's tax is the obvious error. This means they're a temporary visitor to Australia holding a subclass 417 (working holiday) or subclass 462 (work and holiday) visa.\" A nonzero value therefore dates a period of visa status as well as a tax amount, and INCM_WHM_GRS_AMT on the same row carries the matching gross.","dsrc":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types","durl":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/income-types","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Working Holiday Maker Total PAYGW Amount - Event payment","k":"PAYG withholding on working holiday maker income, year to date (dollars)","def":"A cumulative dollar amount within the financial year, withheld at the working holiday maker scale, which begins at 15 cents in the dollar on the first band of income rather than at the resident tax-free threshold.","p":"2020 to 2025-2026","s":"sourced","src":"ATO, Single Touch Payroll Phase 2 employer reporting guidelines, Income types","url":"https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/hiring-and-paying-your-workers/single-touch-payroll/in-detail/single-touch-payroll-phase-2-employer-reporting-guidelines/reporting-the-amounts-you-have-paid/income-types","lim":"It covers only the part of the year the person was reported as a working holiday maker.
